thread:
anya: heads-up — onboarding Serendipity13B (hf/serendipity/13b) into int4 pipeline uncovered a weird rotary alignment regression after tokenization normalization. reproducible locally. :bug:
anya: steps: convert hf -> our-onnx -> quant-int4, run generate with long context (2k), compare logits vs fp16 baseline. approx 0.8% token-level mismatch concentrated around tokens containing soft-hyphen / combining diacritics.
anya: quick log excerpt:

```
input: "I was going to co\u00ad-operate with the team"  # note soft-hyphen 
fp16 next token logits top3: [0.23, 0.12, 0.07]
int4 next token logits top3: [0.16, 0.18, 0.11]
kv-cache head 3 rotary angles differ by ~0.0025 radians at positions where token contains U+00AD or combining marks
```

jun: :eyes: interesting. do we see same behavior on other models or just Serendipity? is tokenizer config using nfkc or no?

anya: i ran quick tests vs Gemma-lite and Qwen-small — they don't show this magnitude of divergence. Serendipity's tokenizer seems to keep soft-hyphen as separate token in some cases (subword boundary) which shifts token ids by 1 for following tokens, but that alone wouldn't cause rotary angle drift — looks like a rotation index/position mapping bug after quant kernel reorder.

sam: i reproduced. attaching tiny repro (ran on x86 int4 build). snippet: `scripts/repro/serendipity_rotary_mismatch.py` uses `--preserve-soft-hyphen` flag and compares cache angle matrices. i see headwise phase mismatch only after the quant stride packing step.

kendra: fyi tokenizer normalization variant is controlled by `tokenizer.normalization` in the HF config. Serendipity upstream uses NFKC+CaseFold by default but their HF artifact here has an older config that doesn't run normalizer on convert. that explains soft-hyphen being present sometimes. still doesn't fully explain rotary drift after quant. :thinking_face:

rahul: can we bisect where in the pipeline the angle mapping diverges? i.e., after export -> reorder -> quant pack -> runtime load. if it's after quant pack, maybe our packer is assuming contiguous token id mapping per bytepair merge that Serendipity violates (because of zero-width or soft-hyphen produced tokens). run `./tools/cache-diff --left fp16 --right int4 --pos 128` to dump head matrices. i have queued an AD-hoc eval on canary (job 732100-A) to compare perplexity across 1k eval prompts. expected regression ~0.6-1.0% if angles misalign.

ci-bot: build/quant-pack-2026-03-22 FAILED for job 732100-A — reproducer run hit a mismatch threshold. logs: https://ci/reports/732100-A (truncated).

jun: if packer assumes token id contiguous strides, a remapping step should fix. maybe the tokenizer produces alias ids > vocab_size in convert path (we saw this with other models). check `vocab.json` vs `merges.txt` for odd entries like `\u00ad` or combining sequences.

sam: quick experiment: forcing nfkc pre-normalize before tokenization (in repro) removes soft-hyphen token and the int4->fp16 token alignment delta disappears; rotary angles match within 1e-5. so normalization mitigates, but we need to decide whether to apply that transform automatically in conversion or patch quant packer to tolerate noncontiguous id spaces.

kendra: patch option matrix:
- short term: add NFKC normalizer option to our conversion CLI and enable for Serendipity (low risk).
- medium: update conversion tests to run token-level canonicalization checks (ensures no stray control/soft-hyphen tokens).
- long: make packer robust to sparse token id allocation (nonlinear mapping).

anya: agreed. plan: 1) enable nfkc pre-normalize in conversion for this model and rerun int4 job (low-risk, quick). 2) open follow-up issue to harden packer and add regression tests (ticket INF-1732). 3) run full eval suite comparing rollout baseline.

rahul: i'll kick off the canary eval once nfkc-run completes. also +1 on adding a canonicalizer lint to the conversion CI.

anya: assigning myself to quick conversion change. i'll post results here when ci passes. thanks all :thumbsup:
